hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: A single work-item path-scheme module becomes the sole authority on where a work item's artifacts live. It is built on a uniform work-item identity — the existing canonical WorkflowId, fixed so every story-id form (lowercase s1 and uppercase S001) canonicalizes the same way — and maps that identity plus a human slug to a nested, work-item-first tree: docs/epics/<slug>-E<date><hash8>/ for epic-parented work and docs/standalone/<slug>-E<date><hash8>/ for triage-routed features, each holding item-root artifacts (SPEC/DEF/HLD) at its root and per-story S<nnn>/ subfolders (LLD/PLAN/BUILD/CR/EXT). Every per-type path helper delegates to this module and every directory-enumeration / filename-prefix finder is replaced by its listing functions, so the write side and the read side resolve the layout through one definition and can never disagree. The one-time migration reuses the very same resolver to compute each existing file's destination; the hash-flat .insrc/artifacts JSON store is left untouched.

consumedContracts.name: Uniform work-item identity
consumedContracts.purpose: One canonical, both-way identity for every work item and story — epic-parented or standalone — so identity can serve as the folder key and lookup key the whole layout hangs on. Closes the gap where an uppercase-form story id fails to canonicalize and falls back to a bare id.

consumedContracts.name: Work-item artifact path scheme
consumedContracts.purpose: The single authority mapping a work item's identity + human slug to its place in the nested tree, and enumerating the tree. Every artifact writer and every finder routes through it, so the write side and read side share one layout definition; the filename supplies only the human label, never identity.

boundary.internal: Private to S003: the one-time migration script itself — how it reads each file's identity from the insrc:artifact marker + companion .insrc/artifacts JSON meta, its two-direction git-mv relocation, the fail-loud stop-and-report on any file that does not confidently map, the cross-document link rewrite via the move's path-mapping table plus the post-move validation pass, and the per-epic chunked-commit execution (fix-or-rollback the chunk on failure) within the single atomic PR. It produces no contract others consume; it is a throwaway tool that leans on sc1 and sc2.

hldContextSlice.rolloutPhase: Phase C — one-time migration of existing artifacts

nonFunctional.performance: The resolver is pure path construction plus, for listing, a bounded walk of the nested tree — no measurable regression versus today's per-type readdir scans over a repo with ~200 artifacts.
nonFunctional.security: No new surface: the artifact store is filesystem-local and the change adds no external input or network path; identity is read from files the daemon already owns.
nonFunctional.observability: The migration fails loud — every unmappable file is reported by path + reason (k3), and the first cross-document link that does not resolve against the new tree aborts the run with that link named (k4).
nonFunctional.durability: git mv preserves each artifact's version history (k4); the hash-flat .insrc/artifacts JSON store — the canonical machine record — is untouched, so no machine-readable state is at risk in the move.

api.name: planMigration

parameters.name: repoPath
parameters.purpose: repo root holding the flat docs/ tree + the hash-flat .insrc/artifacts store

returns.meaning: Pure (no disk writes, no git): the computed relocation — { moves: {from,to,kind,identity}[]; linkRewrites: {file, from, to}[]; unmappable: {artifactId, reason}[] }. Enumerates the artifact set from .insrc/artifacts/*.json (authoritative — non-artifact hand-written docs never appear), groups by work item (epicHash + standalone flag), derives ONE WorkItemIdentity per group from the group's anchor createdAt (DEF's, or the standalone LLD's) + a slug sourced from a slug-carrying member, and resolves each member's nested destination via resolveArtifactMdPath. Skips artifacts already at their nested destination (idempotent — e.g. S002's own BUILD.md).

postconditions: Pure — no filesystem mutation, no git; safe to call as a dry-run/preview
unmappable[] is non-empty (rather than a partial moves[]) whenever ANY artifact's group lacks an anchor (no DEF/LLD createdAt) or a slug source — the caller fails loud on it (ac2/k3)
Every move's `to` is computed by resolveArtifactMdPath, so writer + migration destinations are identical (k2); identity comes only from companion-JSON metadata, the slug is only a label (k5)

api.name: applyMigration
api.signature: function applyMigration(repoPath: string, plan: MigrationPlan): void

parameters.name: plan
parameters.purpose: the plan from planMigration (must have empty unmappable[])

returns.meaning: The thin executor: refuses if plan.unmappable is non-empty (fail-loud, ac2); git mv each move (history preserved, ac1); apply linkRewrites across moved md via the flat→nested path table; then a post-move validation walks the new tree (listWorkItems/listArtifactMdPaths) and throws if any intra-artifact link fails to resolve (ac3) BEFORE the change is accepted; commits per-epic chunks.

errors.condition: plan.unmappable is non-empty — refuses to apply, naming the unmappable files (ac2/k3)
a post-move cross-document link does not resolve against the new tree — rejects the migration naming the link (ac3/k4)
a git mv fails for a chunk — the chunk is rolled back (fix-or-rollback) rather than leaving a partial mix (lc1)

preconditions: plan produced by planMigration on the same repoPath
the repo is a clean git working tree (git mv operates on tracked files)
postconditions: Every relocated artifact md is under its work item's nested folder with git history intact (ac1); no artifact remains in a flat location once accepted (lc1)
The .insrc/artifacts JSON store is byte-unchanged (only md files move)

api.name: deriveWorkItemIdentity
api.signature: function deriveWorkItemIdentity(epicHash: string, createdAtISO: string, storyId?: string): WorkItemIdentity

parameters.name: epicHash
parameters.purpose: the work item's epic hash (from the artifact id / companion meta)

parameters.name: createdAtISO
parameters.purpose: the work item's ANCHOR createdAt (the group's DEF or standalone-LLD createdAt), shared by every member

parameters.name: storyId
parameters.purpose: story id for a story-scoped artifact; omitted at epic level

returns.meaning: sc1 identity — consumed as-is; the migration calls it ONCE per work item so the epicSegment is shared across the group

errors.condition: propagated on a malformed epicHash/createdAt (surfaced as an unmappable entry, not a crash)

postconditions: Consumed unchanged from sc1 (S001) — S003 owns no part of it

api.name: resolveArtifactMdPath
api.signature: function resolveArtifactMdPath(repoPath: string, identity: WorkItemIdentity, kind: ArtifactKind, workItemKind: WorkItemKind, slug: string): string

parameters.name: kind
parameters.purpose: artifact kind parsed from the id prefix (DEF/HLD/LLD/PLAN/BUILD/CR/SPEC/EXT)

parameters.name: slug
parameters.purpose: the group's shared human slug label

returns.meaning: sc2 nested destination for one artifact — consumed as-is; the migration's `to` path

errorCases.scenario: An artifact's work-item group has no derivable ANCHOR (no DEF and — for a standalone item — no LLD carrying a createdAt) or no derivable SLUG (no member with meta.epicSlug and no slug-named sibling filename).
errorCases.detection: During the per-group identity derivation in planMigration: the group is scanned for an anchor-createdAt source and a slug source; if either is absent the group's members are pushed to unmappable[] with the reason (missing-anchor / missing-slug).
errorCases.response: planMigration returns a non-empty unmappable[] and applyMigration REFUSES to move anything, printing each unmappable artifactId + reason. No partial move (ac2/k3/lc1). The operator fixes the underlying data (or excludes the item) and re-runs.
errorCases.userImpact: The migration halts before touching the tree, naming exactly which work item can't be placed — never a silent misfile or leave-behind.

errorCases.scenario: A companion .insrc/artifacts/<ID>.json exists but its md file is absent at the reconstructed OLD flat path (or is already at the nested destination).
errorCases.detection: planMigration stat()s the reconstructed OLD flat md path for each artifact id; a missing source that is NOT already at its nested destination is recorded (missing-md); one already at the nested destination is SKIPPED (idempotent).
errorCases.response: A genuinely missing md is reported in unmappable[] (halts); an already-nested one is a no-op skip. Never a git mv from a non-existent path.
errorCases.userImpact: A dangling JSON record is surfaced rather than crashing the git mv; a re-run over an already-migrated tree is a clean no-op.

errorCases.scenario: After moving, a cross-document link inside a relocated md still points at a path that does not exist in the new tree.
errorCases.detection: applyMigration's post-move validation pass walks the new tree via sc2 listWorkItems/listArtifactMdPaths and resolves every intra-artifact md link (after the flat→nested rewrite table is applied); an unresolved link is caught here, BEFORE the change is accepted.
errorCases.response: The migration is REJECTED (throws, naming the file + the broken link) and the chunk is rolled back — the accepted state never contains a broken link (ac3/k4).
errorCases.userImpact: A link the rewrite missed aborts the run with the exact link named, rather than shipping a broken-link tree.

errorCases.scenario: A git mv fails mid-chunk (e.g. a destination path collision, or the working tree was not clean).
errorCases.detection: applyMigration checks the working tree is clean before starting and checks each git mv's exit status; a non-zero status aborts the current per-epic chunk.
errorCases.response: The failing chunk is rolled back (git reset/checkout of that chunk) so the repo is never left in a partial-mix state (lc1); the error names the chunk + the failing move. Other already-committed chunks stand (per-epic chunked commits).
errorCases.userImpact: A failure is contained to one epic's chunk and reversed, not smeared across the whole tree.

edgeCases.expected: It has no entry in the .insrc/artifacts store, so planMigration never enumerates it — it is left in place, neither moved nor reported as unmappable (only real artifacts can be unmappable).

invariantsToPreserve.text: The hash-flat .insrc/artifacts JSON store is byte-unchanged — the migration moves ONLY md files; no companion JSON is renamed, rewritten, or moved (it is the machine record + the migration's own input set).
A work item's identity (epicHash + story ordinal + anchor createdAt) is derived ONLY from companion-JSON metadata; the filename contributes only the human slug label (k5).

One anchor createdAt per work item (the DEF's, or the standalone LLD's) is shared across every member — never each file's own companion createdAt — so a work item can never split across UTC-day folders (the S002 folder-anchor model).
Every destination is computed by sc2's resolveArtifactMdPath, so the migration and the live writer produce identical folders (k2); the migration adds no second path grammar.

Cross-document md→md links are rare (3, all in a hand-written non-artifact doc that is not moved), so the link-rewrite + post-move validation surface is small and fully checkable against the new tree before accept (ac3/k4).

migrationSteps.action: Land the migration code: add src/workflow/migrate-docs-tree.ts (pure planMigration + thin applyMigration built on sc1/sc2) + a bin entry + its unit/integration tests. Purely additive — no production code depends on it, nothing on disk moves yet.

Run planMigration(repoPath) as a DRY-RUN and inspect the printed moves[]/linkRewrites[]/unmappable[]. If unmappable[] is non-empty, STOP and fix the underlying data (or explicitly exclude an item) before proceeding — nothing has moved (ac2/k3). Fully rollbackable (read-only).

On a clean git working tree, run applyMigration per-epic in CHUNKS: for each work item, git mv every member md to its nested destination (history preserved, ac1), then commit that epic's chunk. A chunk whose git mv fails is rolled back (git reset/checkout) leaving no partial mix; other committed chunks stand.
Rewrite any intra-artifact cross-document link via the flat→nested path-mapping table built from the moves (in practice a near-empty set per the link bundle), staged within the same chunk commits.

Run the post-move validation pass: walk the new tree via sc2 listWorkItems/listArtifactMdPaths and resolve every intra-artifact link; if ANY link fails to resolve, REJECT the migration (throw, name the link) and roll back the offending chunk BEFORE acceptance (ac3/k4).

Refresh the stale doc/JSDoc/help text that still describes the flat layout (storage.ts already done in S002; artifacts/{plan,hld,lld}.ts headers, runners/tracker help text) so the docs match the now-fully-nested reality. Optionally delete the one-shot migration module. Additive/cosmetic.

migration.backwardCompat: This is a DATA move, not an API change — no function signature changes (the migration only CONSUMES sc1/sc2). The one compatibility consideration: any reference to an artifact by its OLD flat docs path breaks after the move. This is already handled by S002 — gates.jsonPathForMd resolves md→json via the embedded insrc:artifact marker (not the path) and the .insrc/artifacts JSON store (every machine consumer's source of truth) is byte-unchanged, so daemon/CLI/MCP behaviour is unaffected. The only breakage is human bookmarks to a flat docs path; git mv keeps history so `git log --follow` and blame still work. External tools that hardcoded a flat docs path (none known) would need updating — acceptable for a one-time reorg (k1, no shim).

alternativesConsidered.name: JSON-store-driven, work-item-grouped planner + thin git executor
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Enumerate the authoritative artifact set from .insrc/artifacts/<ID>.json, group by work item, derive ONE identity (anchor createdAt + slug) per item, resolve every member via sc2 — a pure planMigration() core + a thin apply(git-mv/link-rewrite/validate) shell.
alternativesConsidered.approach: A pure `planMigration(repoPath): MigrationPlan` iterates the hash-flat `.insrc/artifacts/*.json` store (the authoritative artifact set — hand-written docs never appear there, so non-artifacts are excluded by construction, not by fragile filtering). For each artifact JSON it parses the id (kind + epicHash + storyId) and reads meta. It GROUPS by work item (epicHash, and standalone-vs-epic from meta.standalone). Per group it derives ONE WorkItemIdentity: the anchor createdAt = the group's DEF meta.createdAt (or, for a standalone item, the standalone LLD's createdAt), and the slug = the epicSlug from a slug-carrying member (DEF/HLD/LLD/PLAN meta.epicSlug, or parsed from that member's slug-named flat filename) — bridging the gap that BUILD/CR companion JSON lack epicSlug. It then computes each member's OLD flat md path (from the current *ArtifactPaths naming) and NEW nested path via `resolveArtifactMdPath(identity, kind, workItemKind, slug)`, emitting a `{from,to}` move + any link rewrites. It records `unmappable[]` for any artifact whose group has no DEF/anchor or no slug source (fail-loud, ac2). A separate thin `applyMigration(plan)` executor does `git mv` per move (history, ac1), rewrites the flat→nested path table across all moved md, and runs a post-move validation walking the new tree via `listWorkItems`/`listArtifactMdPaths` (rejecting if any intra-artifact link fails to resolve, ac3), committing per-epic chunks. The { json } store is never touched.
pros: The .insrc/artifacts store IS the artifact set — non-artifact hand-written docs (the 3 review audits, docs/workflow.md, plan docs) are excluded with zero filtering, so they are never at risk of a wrong move or a spurious fail-loud (the realism-note winner).

Grouping per work item lets the anchor createdAt + slug be computed ONCE and shared, so every member lands in ONE folder — structurally prevents the S002 split-across-UTC-days bug and bridges the missing-epicSlug gap.
The pure planMigration core makes dry-run, fail-loud, and link-resolution fully unit-testable off a seeded fixture; the git executor is a thin, separately-tested shell.
Reuses sc1+sc2 verbatim (deriveWorkItemIdentity + resolveArtifactMdPath) so writer and migration compute identical destinations (k2).
cons: Must reconstruct each artifact's OLD flat md path from its id/kind (the inverse of the retired flat *ArtifactPaths naming) — a small amount of legacy-naming knowledge encoded in the planner.
BUILD/CR md are markerless, so the planner keys them purely off the JSON id + filename convention, not a self-describing marker.

alternativesConsidered.name: docs-dir-walk planner (readdir the flat dirs, marker/ filename → identity, skip non-artifacts)
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Walk the six flat docs dirs, read each md's insrc:artifact marker (or BUILD/CR filename) → companion JSON, explicitly SKIP files with no marker and no companion, same per-item grouping.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Same grouped-identity + sc2 resolution + thin executor as a1, but the enumeration DRIVES FROM THE DOCS TREE: readdir docs/{defines,designs,plans,builds,specs,reviews}, and for each md read its marker (198 have it) or match a BUILD/CR filename, then look up the companion JSON. A file with neither marker nor a recognized artifact filename+companion is classified NON-ARTIFACT and skipped (left in place). Grouping/anchor/slug logic is identical to a1.
pros: Operates on what the user actually sees (the docs tree), so the move set maps 1:1 to visible files.
The marker is a self-describing signal for the 198 marked files.
cons: Requires an explicit, fragile non-artifact classifier (no marker AND no companion) that must correctly SKIP the 3 review audits + hand-written plan docs while still catching a genuinely-unmappable artifact — the exact judgement a1 avoids by construction.
Mixed identity sources (marker for most, filename for BUILD, skip-heuristic for the rest) is more branching and more ways to misclassify.
Still needs the same grouping to get the anchor/slug, so it is not simpler than a1 — only more error-prone on the artifact-vs-doc boundary.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Functionally equivalent once the input set is correct, but it must reconstruct the artifact-vs-doc boundary with a heuristic classifier that a1 gets for free from the JSON store — partial on ac2/k3 with no offsetting benefit.

alternativesConsidered.name: Per-file independent resolution (no work-item grouping)
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Resolve each artifact's destination independently from its OWN companion createdAt + kind, no per-item anchor sharing.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Iterate the artifact set (either source) and for each file call deriveWorkItemIdentity(epicHash, THIS file's meta.createdAt, storyId) + resolveArtifactMdPath, moving it — with no cross-file grouping to establish a shared anchor or slug.
pros: Simplest control flow — a flat map over files with no grouping pass.
No dependency on a DEF existing before its siblings are placed.
cons: RE-INTRODUCES the S002 folder-split bug: an epic's DEF (day-1) and its BUILD (day-2) compute different E<date> segments → the work item scatters across two folders, directly violating ac1's 'its work item's grouped folder' and lc1's no-partial-mix.

Cannot supply the folder SLUG for BUILD/CR (their companion JSON lacks epicSlug) — they would fall back to a hash label while their DEF/LLD siblings use the real slug, producing a DIFFERENT folder name for the same work item (a second split).
Fails the very goal of the story (one grouped folder per work item).
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Violates ac1 + k1 (folder split from per-file anchor + missing-slug fallback) — it fails the story's core goal; the simpler control flow is not worth a broken end state.
